narrative.overview:
Each lesson is one numbered engineering worksheet: a white sheet outlined in near-black ink, opened by a ruled header strip, and read in a calm serif column. The sheets sit on a plain, quiet neutral frame (the index rail and the outer margin) that recedes so the sheet reads first. Everything on the sheet is drawn the way a careful engineer would draw it by hand: hairline rules, tick boxes, boxed answers, numbered figures, blue pen for links and marks, and a single red mark for where you are and what comes next.

Legibility comes before atmosphere. Text sits on flat, untextured surfaces at high contrast: near-black ink on white for reading, and a dark secondary gray that still clears AA comfortably on the sheet, the frame, and the answer boxes. Nothing patterned, gradiented, or tinted ever sits behind text. This holds everywhere, including the worked-numbers callout.

Density is moderate and steady. The reading column is fixed, the furniture around it is compact and set in a narrow grotesque, and numbers are set in mono or tabular figures so tallies line up. Surfaces are flat inks on paper, separated by rules rather than by depth.
keyCharacteristics: A plain neutral frame and a white sheet; no textures anywhere.
Near-black ink, blue ballpoint for links and marks, one reserved red.
Square corners and 1px rules everywhere; state shown by mark shape.
Archivo condensed for structure, Literata for reading, JetBrains Mono for numbers.
Numbered sheets, numbered figures, numbered sections in the margin.

rules.name: The Clear Ground Rule
rules.body: Text always sits on a flat, solid surface at high contrast. No grids, patterns, gradients, tints, or images behind text, on the frame, the sheet, or any callout. Body text stays near-black on white; secondary text never drops below the Secondary Ink value.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red marks position and the next step, nothing else. Never use it for errors, emphasis, decoration, or a second action on the same screen.

rules.name: The Ink Structure Rule
rules.body: Structural edges (sheet, strip, table, figure, callout, quiz, pager) are Ink; dividers inside them are Hairline. Colour never separates surfaces on its own.

rules.name: The Counted Things Rule
rules.body: Anything counted (sheet numbers, tallies, scores, worked numbers, figure numbers) is set in mono or with tabular figures, zero padded to two digits where it is a sheet number.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo for the worksheet furniture, Literata for the reading. Body prose is never set in Archivo, and structure is never set in Literata. The worked-numbers callout is furniture and stays in Archivo.

rules.name: The Fixed Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text holds at 66ch at every width that can afford it. Wider sheets gain margin, not line length.

rules.name: The Paper Not Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit on the page; they do not hover above it. Use a rule, a fill change to Answer Box, or a heavier border to separate, never a blur shadow, gradient fill, or translucency on content.

rules.name: The Mark Shape Rule
rules.body: State and type are told apart by shape, never colour alone: a drawn tick for done, a struck cross and strikethrough for a wrong answer, and a distinct drawn shape (solid square, triangle, hollow circle, short dash, double bar) before each callout label.

dos: Do keep every surface flat and solid: quiet frame, white sheet, Answer Box. Text always sits on one of them.
Do keep body text Ink on White Sheet and secondary text no lighter than Secondary Ink.
Do draw every edge as a 1px Ink or Hairline rule, and keep corners square.
Do number things: sheets (two digits), sections in the margin, figures per sheet.
Do keep figures inline at a legible size and let wide ones scroll with a caption hint.
Do set every count in mono or tabular figures.
Do give every new state a distinct mark shape before giving it a colour.
Do swap tokens in place for dark mode, using the neutral gray `*-dark` values.
donts: Don't put grids, patterns, gradients, tinted washes, or images behind text anywhere, including callouts and the frame.
Don't tint the frame or sheet with a hue; the neutrals stay near-gray.
Don't use Margin Red for anything other than the current position and the single next action.
Don't use blur shadows, gradients, or translucent content surfaces.
Don't round containers; circles belong to marks only.
Don't set reading prose in Archivo or let the reading column exceed 66ch.
Don't put small uppercase labels above headings; the only small labels are the field names inside header strip cells.
Don't turn the home into a card grid; sheets are listed as numbered rows.
